items.question: Are generated addresses verified physical locations?
items.answer: No. Addresses are assembled algorithmically from bundled geographic databases using valid postal code formats and regional naming conventions. Any coincidence with real residential or commercial premises is unintended.

items.question: Do US ZIP codes correspond to the generated state?
items.answer: Yes. The generator checks a state-to-ZIP prefix lookup table so that California addresses receive 90001–96162, New York gets 10001–14925, and Texas gets 75001–79999.

items.question: Which countries are supported?
items.answer: The generator supports the United States, United Kingdom (correct outward/inward postcode formats), Canada (FSA LDU pattern), Australia, and India (6-digit PIN codes).

items.question: Can I export addresses to CSV or JSON?
items.answer: Yes. You can instantly export up to 50 addresses at a time to comma-separated CSV or structured JSON format.

items.question: Can I use these addresses for actual shipping or orders?
items.answer: Strictly no. These addresses are intended solely for development testing and design mockups. Never use them for real billing, shipping, or government submissions.

items.question: How are UK postcodes validated?
items.answer: UK postcodes follow royal mail structural conventions consisting of an outward code area and district, followed by an inward sector and unit code (e.g., NW1 6XE).

items.question: Can I generate consistent addresses across tests?
items.answer: Yes. Supplying a numeric seed generates identical address lists across multiple browser sessions, enabling reliable test fixtures.

items.question: What variety of street names and types are generated?
items.answer: The engine combines common regional thoroughfare names with appropriate street types (Avenue, Boulevard, Road, Lane, Way, Crescent) for realistic aesthetics.
